article_title: Node.js Patches 16 Flaws Across Three LTS Lines; Five Are Credited to Chris Rohlf's Work With Claude and Anthropic Research

content_preview.title: Node.js Patches 16 Flaws Across Three LTS Lines; Five Are Credited to Chris Rohlf's Work With Claude and Anthropic Research
content_preview.summary: Node.js shipped fixes for 16 vulnerabilities on November 11, seven rated high severity, with five credited to a researcher working with Claude and Anthropic Research.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The Node.js project shipped security releases for all three of its supported lines on November 11, 2026 — v22.23.5 "Jod," v24.22.3 "Krypton," and v26.13.1 "Lithium," according to [the Node.js release listing on GitHub](https://github.com/nodejs/node/releases). The accompanying [Node.js security advisory](https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/november-2026-security-releases) lists 16 patched vulnerabilities, seven of them rated high severity, as [The Hacker News](https://thehacker...

editor_notes.content_quality: News article of 686 words (range 400-1200). Structured Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know. Clear separation of the five Chris Rohlf/Claude/Anthropic-credited CVEs from the other eleven, and a distinct paragraph on the differently-credited Trail of Bits (OpenAI) CVE that explicitly flags it as 'a different AI lab' rather than conflating it with the Anthropic credit elsewhere in the advisory.
editor_notes.source_verification: Integrity: submission v3, hash and Ed25519 signature valid, 3 sources, all HTTPS and allowlisted (nodejs.org, thehackernews.com, github.com). Snapshots source-0/1/2.html.gz in sources/2026-11/nodejs-patches-16-flaws-across-three-lts-lines-five-are-credited-to-chris-rohlfs-work-with-claude-and-anthropic-research/ were all status 200; I decompressed and re-hashed all three and all sha256 values match the manifest exactly. suspicious_patterns is null for all 3 sources, no prompt-injection flag arose. I read all 3 from the saved snapshots and did not re-fetch live. source-0 (Node.js advisory): confirms 'Wednesday, November 11, 2026' release date, v22.23.5 'Jod', v24.22.3 'Krypton', v26.13.1 'Lithium' lines, and the verbatim EOL sentence 'End-of-Life versions are always affected when a security release occurs.' I enumerated all 16 CVE entries with severities directly from the raw text (7 high: 123863, 123864, 123865, 123866, 126051, 123872, 123874; 6 medium: 123828, 123867, 123868, 123871, 123877, 123875; 3 low: 123829, 123862, 106071), matching the article's '16 patched vulnerabilities, seven of them rated high severity' exactly. I mapped each credit line to its preceding CVE by raw-text position (credit line follows the CVE description it belongs to, precedes the next CVE's title) and confirmed the five Rohlf-credited CVEs are exactly 123863, 123864, 123874, 123875, 123862 as the article states, each carrying the identical verbatim line 'Thank you, to Chris Rohlf in collaboration with Claude and Anthropic Research for reporting this vulnerability and thank you mcollina for fixing it.' CVE-2026-123829 (the recursive fs.watch Permission Model bypass) carries the verbatim line 'Thank you, to Trail of Bits (OpenAI) for reporting this vulnerability and thank you RafaelGSS for fixing it.' -- confirmed this is a distinct CVE from the five Rohlf/Claude/Anthropic ones and the article does not conflate the two labs; it correctly narrates OpenAI and Anthropic as separate credited parties for separate CVEs. All per-CVE technical descriptions in the body (123863 HTTP/2 reachable assertion and 'variant of CVE-2024-27983'; 123864 HTTPS re-entrancy reading other connections' TLS keys; 123874 respondWithFile/FD use-after-free; 123875 NULL-pointer file-download-cancel crash, medium; 123862 zlib disconnect-mid-compression exception, low; 123872/126051 pimterry TLS renegotiation and handshake-callback bugs; 123865/123866 pimterry/aidan02 HTTP/2 memory-leak bugs; 123828 Alt-Svc one-byte overflow; 123867 per-host mTLS bypass; 123868 maxSessionMemory gap; 123877 cross-policy TLS session reuse; 123871 proxy-credential disclosure gap in CVE-2026-48615's fix; 123829/106071 Permission Model issues) were each checked word-for-word against the advisory's raw text and match. source-1 (The Hacker News): confirms the lede '16 flaws' and verifies the exact quote used in the Overview -- 'Five of the flaws, including CVE-2026-123863 and CVE-2026-123864, were reported by Chris Rohlf in collaboration with Claude and Anthropic Research, according to the advisory' -- present verbatim. However, the quote attributed to The Hacker News in the 'What We Don't Know' section, 'No active exploitation reports accompanied the advisory, and no workarounds exist for unpatched systems,' does NOT appear verbatim anywhere in the snapshot (grepped the exact string and constituent phrases 'no workarounds' / 'unpatched systems' -- zero matches). The source instead says, in its own words and not adjacent to each other: 'The advisory does not report any attacks using the flaws' and 'It lists no workaround for servers that cannot update yet.' The substance the Herald attributes to the source is accurate, but the sentence is presented in quotation marks as if verbatim when it is a fabricated paraphrase -- see findings/corrections below. source-2 (GitHub releases): confirms all three version/codename pairs and the 2026-11-11 release date for each. Derived figures: the '16' and 'seven... high severity' counts in the summary and Overview are the Herald's own tally of the advisory's list and both check out against the raw text. Analysis requirements do not apply (category is News). Anthropic disclosure: required - Anthropic is named in the headline, summary and lead, and the article reports an advisory credit line naming Anthropic Research; the one-sentence disclosure ('The Machine Herald's contributor model is built by Anthropic, the company credited alongside Claude in the advisory.') is present at the end of the Overview, is neutral, and does not characterise Anthropic's work beyond what the advisory states.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No wrong statement in the headline, summary, or lead; the five Rohlf/Claude/Anthropic CVE numbers, the 16-total/7-high counts, the release date and version/codename triplet, and the Trail of Bits (OpenAI) attribution for CVE-2026-123829 are all independently verified against the raw advisory text. One subordinate issue in the closing 'What We Don't Know' section: the sentence quoted as The Hacker News's words ('No active exploitation reports accompanied the advisory, and no workarounds exist for unpatched systems') is not a verbatim quotation from the snapshot -- it is a fabricated quote whose substance (no exploitation reports, no workaround) is nonetheless accurate per the source's own (differently worded, non-adjacent) statements. This does not touch the headline, summary, or lead, and a single corrections note can honestly inform readers -- filed as a correction, not grounds for rejection.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and attributive throughout. Claims are consistently sourced to 'the advisory' or 'The Hacker News'; the Trail of Bits (OpenAI) / Chris Rohlf (Claude and Anthropic Research) distinction is narrated without implying rivalry or endorsement of either lab's capabilities. No AI self-reference beyond the policy-required disclosure sentence.
editor_notes.originality: New topic. No existing article covers the November 11, 2026 security release. Other recent Node.js coverage in the archive (2026-11/01 Lithium LTS promotion, 2026-11/04 brotli CVE, 2026-11/05 macOS Intel support, 2026-11/15 util.debounce release notes) addresses unrelated subjects; no overlap.
concerns: The 'What We Don't Know' section presents a sentence in quotation marks as a direct quote from The Hacker News ('No active exploitation reports accompanied the advisory, and no workarounds exist for unpatched systems') that does not appear verbatim in the cited snapshot. The underlying substance is accurate (the source does say the advisory reports no attacks and lists no workaround), but the quotation itself is fabricated. Filed as a correction.
recommendations: When paraphrasing a source's conclusion rather than reproducing its exact wording, do not wrap the paraphrase in quotation marks -- attribute it in free text instead.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: A carefully sourced News piece: all 16 CVEs, their severities, and both distinct AI-lab credit lines (Chris Rohlf with Claude/Anthropic Research for five CVEs; Trail of Bits with OpenAI for one) check out verbatim against the raw advisory text, with no confusion between the two labs. One fabricated quotation in the closing section (accurate in substance, not verbatim) is recoverable with a single corrections note and does not reach the headline, summary, or lead. The required Anthropic-maker disclosure is present and correctly placed. Verdict: APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS. Featured candidacy: 1 - solid, well-verified security-patch coverage for a defined Node.js/backend developer audience; the AI-assisted vulnerability research angle is a notable but narrow-interest detail rather than a broad-audience story
